title: What ethics training must US federal employees complete?
description: 5 CFR Part 2638, Subpart C: initial ethics training within 3 months, annual training for disclosure filers, and live training rules, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: Under 5 CFR Part 2638, Subpart C, issued by the US Office of Government Ethics (OGE), every new executive branch employee subject to the Standards of Conduct must complete interactive initial ethics training within 3 months of appointment. Public and confidential financial disclosure filers, contracting officers and some other employees must also complete at least 1 hour of annual ethics training each calendar year, with live training required for the most senior officials. These rules apply as at November 2026.
keyTakeaways: 5 CFR 2638.304: each new employee must complete initial ethics training within 3 months of appointment, in an interactive format, covering financial conflicts of interest, impartiality, misuse of position and gifts.

5 CFR 2638.307 and 2638.308: confidential filers, public filers, presidential appointees, Executive Office of the President staff and contracting officers complete annual ethics training before the end of each calendar year, with 1 hour of duty time.

Public filers paid at Level I or II of the Executive Schedule need 1 hour of live training every year; other civilian officials named in section 103(c) of the Ethics in Government Act and stationed in the United States need live training every 2 years; all remaining public filers train interactively.
Senate-confirmed appointees receive an additional live ethics briefing no later than 15 days after appointment under 5 CFR 2638.305.
5 CFR 2638.301 states that an agency's failure to deliver training does not exempt any employee from ethics requirements.
regulator: US Office of Government Ethics (OGE), with each agency's Designated Agency Ethics Official (DAEO)
appliesTo: New executive branch employees subject to the Standards of Ethical Conduct (5 CFR Part 2635)
Public financial disclosure filers (annual public reports under 5 CFR 2634.201(a))
Confidential financial disclosure filers (5 CFR 2634.904), presidential appointees, Executive Office of the President employees and contracting officers
New supervisors (written notice) and agency ethics staff (DAEO-defined training)

sections.heading: Which rules set federal ethics training requirements?

blocks.text: Subpart C of [5 CFR Part 2638](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-5/part-2638/subpart-C), Government Ethics Training, sets the education requirements for the executive branch ethics program. Section 2638.301 states that "every agency must carry out a government ethics education program to teach employees how to identify government ethics issues and obtain assistance in complying with ethics laws and regulations."

OGE writes the rules and each agency's Designated Agency Ethics Official (DAEO) runs the program. Section 2638.309 allows the DAEO to add agency-specific training for groups of employees and requires the DAEO to make sure staff who perform ethics duties have the necessary expertise. These rules sit alongside, not inside, other annual federal training obligations such as [cybersecurity awareness](/regulations/federal-employee-cybersecurity-awareness-training) and [records management](/regulations/nara-records-management-training-requirements).

blocks.title: No exemption for missed training
blocks.text: 5 CFR 2638.301: "An agency's failure to comply with any of the education or notice requirements set forth in this subpart does not exempt an employee from applicable government ethics requirements."

sections.heading: What does initial ethics training require?

blocks.text: Every new employee subject to the Standards of Conduct must complete interactive initial ethics training within 3 months of appointment. Section 2638.304 applies to anyone appointed to an agency position who was not an employee of that agency immediately before.

items: **Content:** the presentation must address financial conflicts of interest, impartiality, misuse of position and gifts. Written materials must include the OGE summary of the Standards of Conduct or an agency equivalent, relevant supplemental agency regulations and ethics office contact instructions.

**Exclusion:** the DAEO may exclude a non-supervisory position at or below GS-8 from the presentation if the DAEO signs a written determination that the duties do not create a substantial likelihood of conflicts of interest and the position is not a confidential filing position. The employee still receives the written materials within 3 months.
**Nominees:** a presidential nominee for a Senate-confirmed position may complete the training before or after appointment, but not later than 3 months after it.

**Prospective employees:** section 2638.303 requires written job offers for covered positions to state the agency's commitment to ethics, notice of the Standards of Conduct and criminal conflict of interest statutes, and, where applicable, the time frame for initial training.

sections.heading: What counts as interactive or live ethics training?

blocks.text: The two formats are defined in 5 CFR 2638.302, and the definitions decide whether an e-learning module satisfies the rule. Training is **interactive** if the employee "is required to take an action with regard to the subject of the training," and that action must use knowledge gained from the training. It "may not be limited to merely advancing from one section of the training to another section."

Training is **live** if "the presenter personally communicates a substantial portion of the material at the same time as the employees being trained are receiving the material." It can be delivered in person or by video or audio technology, and the presenter must answer questions during the session and explain how to submit questions afterwards. Live training also satisfies the interactive requirement. A click-through module with no knowledge checks meets neither definition, which matters when choosing [assessment methods](/guides/how-to-design-competency-assessments).

sections.heading: Who needs annual ethics training and in what format?

blocks.text: Annual training applies to financial disclosure filers and certain other designated employees, not to the whole workforce. Each covered employee must finish before the end of the calendar year, and agencies must give 1 hour of duty time.

blocks.text: For live annual training of public filers, section 2638.308(c) requires the presenter to have knowledge of government ethics laws and regulations and to be qualified, as the DAEO deems appropriate, to answer basic and advanced questions. Limited exceptions exist: the Level I and II live requirement can be replaced with interactive training if a matter of vital national interest requires it, and the DAEO may give written authorization in extraordinary circumstances for a section 103(c) employee due for live training to train interactively that year.

sections.heading: How must completion be tracked and coordinated?

blocks.text: Annual training must be confirmed in writing, and large agencies must confirm that delegated offices are following the procedures. Under sections 2638.307 and 2638.308, the employee confirms completion in writing, a presenter with knowledge of completion may record it, or the DAEO may accept automatic tracking by the system that delivered interactive training.

Section 2638.310 applies to agencies with 1,000 or more employees. Any office outside the DAEO's supervision that issues ethics notices or delivers initial training must submit to the DAEO, by January 15 each year, a written summary of its procedures and written confirmation that there is a reasonable basis to conclude they have been implemented. For record design, see [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps the four required subjects, the agency's supplemental regulations and its ethics agreements to learning outcomes and to the populations defined in Subpart C, so each filer category's format and frequency are explicit. Assessment points are designed to meet the interactive definition rather than simple page advancement. For other public sector obligations, see [government and defense](/industries/government-defence).

faqs.q: Do all federal employees need annual ethics training?
faqs.a: No. Under Subpart C, annual training is required for public and confidential financial disclosure filers, presidential appointees, Executive Office of the President employees, contracting officers and anyone else the agency head designates. Other employees complete initial training within 3 months of appointment, though a DAEO may add agency-specific requirements under 5 CFR 2638.309.

faqs.q: Does a self-paced online module count as interactive ethics training?
faqs.a: It can, if employees must take an action that uses what they learned, such as answering scenario questions with feedback. 5 CFR 2638.302 says the required action may not be limited to advancing from one section to the next, so a module that only needs clicks through pages does not qualify.

faqs.q: Do federal contractors have to complete OGE ethics training?
faqs.a: Subpart C applies to agency employees, not to contractor staff. Contractor personnel are governed by their employer's own program and by any training their contract imposes, not by OGE's training rules. Note that federal contracting officers, who are agency employees, are named in 5 CFR 2638.307 as an annual training population.

faqs.q: What happens if an agency fails to deliver required ethics training?
faqs.a: The employee is still bound. 5 CFR 2638.301 states that an agency's failure to meet the education or notice requirements does not exempt an employee from applicable government ethics requirements. The agency's program shortfall is a separate matter for the DAEO and OGE oversight.
